newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up on dollar sales by banks.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up on dollar sales by banks.

text.p: The Indian rupee recovered strongly from an early fall to end Friday at 35.68/70 per dollar after touching a low of 35.76 in active trade, dealers said.
The rupee had opened Friday at 35.72/74 per dollar.
"Some sustained buying by a large state-run bank in the morning pushed the rupee down to 35.76," a dealer said. "But once it withdrew from the market, the rupee began to recover."

Dealers said good dollar supplies in the afternoon helped the rupee recover. "Banks were selling on behalf of companies and also liquidating their long positions," a dealer said. "Some banks had gone long anticipating continued dollar purchases from a state-run bank."
"But once it stopped buying the market, they sold dollars and the rupee recovered."
Dealers said premia on forward dollars maintained the easy trend of the last few days. The premia for six-month dollars ended Friday at 9.14 percent against Thursday's 9.30 percent, they said.
